name: Private-press book
region: Hammersmith, London, then Germany and the United States
summary: A book printed by hand on handmade paper, in a heavy type cut for the press, with woodcut borders and initials, in black and red. William Morris started the Kelmscott Press in 1891 against the grey, thin books of the steam press; the Doves Press made the same craft plain.

philosophy.core_thesis: A book is one object: the type, the page, the paper, the ink and the ornament are made together and by hand.
design_principles: Set a dense, dark text page in one heavy roman or gothic type, with little space between the words and the lines.
Use the two pages of an opening as one unit, with margins in the ratio 2:3:4:6 (inner, top, outer, bottom).
Print in a deep black and use red for the headings, the shoulder notes and the initials.
Frame the first page with a woodcut border of leaves and flowers, and start each part with a woodcut initial.
Print on handmade rag paper or vellum, with a clear bite of the type into the sheet.
Bind in plain vellum or linen; the decoration is inside the book, not on the cover.
anti_patterns: Thin, grey type on a smooth, coated paper
Wide spaces between words that make rivers
A photographic image or a halftone
Equal margins on all four sides

process.matrix: Metal type cast for the press (Golden, Troy, Doves Type) and woodcut blocks for borders and pictures.
process.press: An iron hand press (Albion), worked by two pressmen.
process.image_making: The designer draws the borders and initials; a wood engraver cuts them; the compositors set the text by hand.
process.edition: Some 200–500 paper copies and a few on vellum.

inks.strategy: A dense black ink that Morris had made to order, and a vermilion for the rubrics.

screening.rule: Make the tone only with the white-on-black and black-on-white lines of the woodcut.

registration.rule: The red prints in a second pull; it must sit exactly in its place in the text.

substrate.stock: Handmade linen paper (Batchelor) with a watermark, or vellum.
substrate.finish: Laid, with deckle edges, dampened before the print.

surface.impression: A clear bite of the type and the cuts into the damp paper.
surface.texture: A dark, even page of type framed in white, with dense leaf ornament.

marks: a red rubric in the text
a colophon with the press mark

emotion.target_response: Respect for the craft: the reader feels the weight and the care of a book made to last.

avoid_when: The reader must scan the text fast.

modifiers.how: Keep the hand press and the paper, but drop the borders and set the text in a light Venetian roman, as the Doves Press did.
Change the book page for a broadside of stacked display type in black and red.

sources.title: William S. Peterson, The Kelmscott Press: A History of William Morris's Typographical Adventure (Clarendon, 1991)
